selectedNativeTransport.variant: In-process C/C++ Node-API addon; AF_UNIX SOCK_SEQPACKET to a fixed root-owned native receiver on the same Linux kernel
selectedNativeTransport.runtimeBaselineProposed: Node24.21.0; Linux6.12+ with verified SO_PASSCRED, SO_PASSPIDFD and pidfs identity; unsupported features deny, no STREAM/SO_PEERCRED-only fallback

mechanics.sourceProtocolChange: Select SEQPACKET carrier for this distinct retention proposal. Do not repurpose V5 method labels/schema/ACK or imply draft STREAM carrier was implemented.
mechanics.frame: One SOCK_SEQPACKET packet is exactly one bounded 1..16384-byte UTF8 JSON envelope. No redundant 4-byte stream length prefix in this selected source revision. Reject truncation, malformed UTF8, duplicates, unknown ancillary data and unexpected FDs.
mechanics.receive: Enable SO_PASSCRED and SO_PASSPIDFD before messages on both sides; accept exactly one SCM_CREDENTIALS and one nonnegative kernel-generated SCM_PIDFD; recvmsg with MSG_CMSG_CLOEXEC; reject MSG_TRUNC/MSG_CTRUNC and all unexpected ancillary data
mechanics.fdCleanup: Never accept SCM_RIGHTS as a runtime identity or application capability. Close every received unexpected FD and each temporary per-message pidfd, even if an earlier close fails; do not stop cleanup at first error. Keep only independently enrolled registry pidfds.
mechanics.nodeNativeBoundary: Native channel object owns FDs and does not expose/accept a caller-selected fd/path/UID/PID/verified flag; typed JS codec receives authenticated response bytes only
mechanics.timeouts: Bound connection/queue/packet waits by monotonic deadlines and bounded queue. Deadline closes only local I/O; never infer cancel/abort/drain or silently replay a destructive call.

peerAndCustody.rootRegistration: Independent root launcher enrolls the actual Node process pidfd, accepted UID/GID and namespaces/cgroup, image/source/bootstrap/SDK pins, exact owner/store/dataset and runtime-generation in protected registry. Caller headers/JSON/stdin cannot enroll or select any of these.
peerAndCustody.perMessageMatch: Check received pidfd is pidfs; compare fstat(st_dev,st_ino) with the root-held registered process pidfd; credentials UID/GID must match their accepted receiver-namespace mapping. Numeric PID is diagnostic, never the process-incarnation key. Per-message pidfd comparison prevents accepted socket FD transfer to a different process from inheriting its sender identity.
peerAndCustody.pidfsBasis: This comparator is inferred from pinned Linux6.12 pidfs source using per-process inode and stashed pid path. Its actual target-kernel behavior remains an acceptance test, not an executed result.
peerAndCustody.serverToNode: Native addon verifies per-response credentials and pidfs identity against a fixed root-owned, app-nonwritable bootstrap record. Connect-time SO_PEERPIDFD may retain server incarnation; every response SCM_PIDFD must match it and the root-selected record. UID0 or pathname permissions alone are not a server attestation.
peerAndCustody.privilegeBoundary: Host root is trusted. Enrolled Node peers must have no credential-forgery capabilities (CAP_SYS_ADMIN/CAP_SETUID/CAP_SETGID in relevant namespaces), no ptrace/host-root/Docker-socket authority, and accepted namespace/custody isolation. SDK install proves none of this.
peerAndCustody.sameProcessExecLimit: pidfd represents process identity and survives same-process exec. CLOEXEC is hygiene, not sufficient execution custody. Root enrollment must accept the actual fixed-launch/no unauthorized re-exec custody policy and source generation mechanism before active admit/permit. This proposal has not implemented or verified such a policy; it does not market pidfd as executable attestation.
peerAndCustody.noCommitLivenessRequirement: Root current-generation decision is needed at admission/permit. An immutable accepted permit may later settle original effects after peer death/exec/revoke; do not require executable/process liveness throughout external SQL COMMIT.

applicationJournalProposal.mutableState: prepared -> committed OR prepared -> sealed_no_effect; terminal states immutable, no reset/replacement or changed cutoff/permit for the same operation ID.
applicationJournalProposal.ownership: Migration-owned immutable binding/state guards and narrow fixed-plan registrar/executor/resolver routines. No general runtime ability to forge committed/sealed rows or delete the ledger. Existing ordinary measurement/revocation privileges are not changed by this proposal.
applicationJournalProposal.committedMarker: Written only by the fixed expiration executor after both DELETE statements in the same original transaction. It binds the exact origin/body/schema/permit and complete table plan; no row count or billing counter substitutes for it.
applicationJournalProposal.sealedMarker: Written only by the fixed origin resolver after taking the same origin row lock and matching the complete immutable binding. It permanently forbids that origin's future destructive entry.
applicationJournalProposal.history: Unresolved or still-referenced origin evidence cannot be removed by the existing expiration plan. This proposal grants no new retention period or automatic evidence purge.

firstExecutionOrder: Accepted owner admission and immutable origin permit must already exist durably before SQL handoff; no local flag or prepared row issues that permit.

Store-owned registrar inserts the exact prepared origin in a short separate durable transaction before destructive BEGIN. Only the worker with positively acknowledged first creation may continue once in this invocation. Existing rows, conflicts, ambiguous insert/registration ACK or process recovery go only to resolveOrigin, never destructive retry.

Original worker begins its one transaction, locks the exact prepared origin row with SELECT FOR UPDATE and rechecks all origin/body/schema/cutoff/permit fields plus open state before any DELETE. A sealed or terminal row denies new effects, including a worker paused before BEGIN or before this lock.

Under that lock, run the two fixed expiration DELETE statements with the same original cutoff; receipt FK cascades delete intervals and ETA in this transaction. Write the committed marker after those effects and COMMIT the same transaction.

Track actual command/transaction-phase observations separately. Never reissue destructive work or COMMIT on unknown. Return only fixed safe lifecycle errors; the consumer retains the original lease/permit pending until independently resolved outcome and exact-origin effect quiescence.
On ambiguous SQL/rollback/connection state request client.release(true) once rather than making the client reusable. Local disposal is not a transaction outcome or independent drain.
resolverOrder: Use the accepted current application-store incarnation/continuity and fresh authoritative primary view; independently resolve the original operation and exact stored binding. Replica/restore/stale or missing-origin evidence stays pending.

Begin a resolver transaction and take the same origin row lock. Timeout/busy/unavailable stays pending. Never treat idle backend, missing active transaction, row count or absent committed marker as abort.

If the committed marker is present and exact, the original four-effect transaction committed. Its terminal state bars later work. Publish/resolve the commit and exact-origin effect-quiescence evidence only after durable fresh readback.

If the exact existing origin remains prepared under the acquired lock with no committed marker, atomically CAS it to sealed_no_effect and commit. This serialization resolves the origin, and the same mandatory entry check rejects a delayed worker. It is no-effects closure, not a claim that a PostgreSQL ROLLBACK command was received.

If resolver COMMIT acknowledgement is lost, keep pending and probe the same original row again; no new operation, permit, cutoff or destructive work. A terminal marker's durable readback can resolve that uncertainty.
Missing original row remains unknown: preparation may still be in flight, evidence may be lost or continuity may be wrong. Absence is never the terminal no-transaction proof.

Quiescence coverage is this exact origin's fixed effect closure: no active origin transaction can pass the common lock and no later original work can enter after the durable terminal seal. It is not proof that a physical backend/session is gone and not owner-wide drain/replay coverage.

sqlObservations.commitAck: Original transaction result must actually carry COMMIT, with corresponding completed protocol/idle observation. A successful Promise alone is insufficient; transaction COMMIT can report a rollback result. Independently resolved durable marker remains the accepted outcome basis.
sqlObservations.knownRollbackObservation: Received original ROLLBACK completion before any COMMIT attempt is a local known-rollback observation; pair it with the exact origin seal/readback for stable no-effect closure. A later ROLLBACK ACK after attempted/lost COMMIT does not prove that original COMMIT failed.
sqlObservations.notStartedObservation: A local failure before BEGIN is not independent no-transaction evidence. Resolve/seal the durable original row, or remain pending if the row/binding is unresolved.
sqlObservations.unknown: Lost COMMIT/ROLLBACK acknowledgement, timeout, disconnect or process death preserves the original pending and permits only origin probing. No compensating assumption, admission restart or blind destructive retry.
